description: Classifies email by direct-to-recipient status, category, action requirement, and urgency. See README.md for the complete processing flow.

direct_to_you.instructions: Was this message written specifically to the recipient as a direct personal or professional communication? A platform-relayed direct message may qualify. General thread comments, repository activity, list posts, campaigns, digests, and system notifications do not qualify merely because a human authored some underlying content.

criteria.yes: A person is directly addressing the recipient in a personal or professional communication.
criteria.no: Not specifically addressed to the recipient, including automated notices, general GitHub activity or thread comments, mailing-list posts, newsletters, campaigns, and system-generated messages.

category.instructions: Classify into exactly one category. HARD RULES: if direct_to_you is yes, category must be personal or work. Any repository, security, account, issue, pull-request, or discussion notification delivered by GitHub is github. Email_lists requires explicit mailing-list evidence such as a List-ID header or known list address; mailing-list subscription, unsubscription, confirmation, command-result, and delivery-failure administration is also email_lists. Parent-facing school or district communications to families are personal. A newsletter requires an identifiable individual author plus a personal first-person author voice; company, brand, team, institutional, or corporate editorial publications are potential_spam. Generic automated social-platform invitation counts, engagement reminders, and network-growth nags are potential_spam; only a person-specific professional invitation or direct message may be work. Nextdoor neighborhood content is potential_spam. Generic commercial recommendations and financial-product promotions such as rate offers or IPO marketing are potential_spam; a specific transactional or user-requested alert may be personal. Optional post-purchase, post-stay, post-appointment, and customer-feedback survey requests are potential_spam; confirmations, receipts, and operational updates remain personal. Generic re-engagement language such as “we miss you,” “we have not seen you,” “come back,” “catch up,” or “see what you missed” is potential_spam even from a trusted service or financial provider; only a specific account, transaction, security, or requested credit-change alert may be personal. Automated LinkedIn notifications are potential_spam by default—including profile updates, position prompts, engagement nudges, summaries, recommendations, and generic invitation notices. Only a genuine person-specific professional invitation or direct message relayed by LinkedIn may be work. An identifiable individual sender or Substack address is not enough for newsletters: unsolicited product launches, vendor announcements, branded pitches, and promotional posts are potential_spam. Generic weekly recaps from commercial or financial services are potential_spam unless they report specific requested account activity. HARD RULES: JavaScript Weekly and comparable established author-curated editorial weeklies are newsletters, not potential_spam. Broad recurring consumer-service reports, club monthly/weekly updates, prayer-request feeds, automated home-value reports, all terms/privacy-policy notices, App Store analytics summaries, and every LinkedIn invitation notification are potential_spam. Guardian insurance messages about claims, coverage, billing, plan documents, account changes, or required benefits actions are personal; generic Guardian wellness/EAP promotions are potential_spam.

criteria.personal: Personal life, family, friends, finances, home, travel, purchases, health, appointments, memberships, clubs, community organizations, household services, children’s schools and activities, and recurring personal activities. Includes legitimate automated member notices, school communications addressed to families, school schedules, event reminders, school bulletins, and specific transactional or user-requested alerts from services the recipient uses. Parent-facing school and district communications to families are Personal even when sent by a staff member or institution. Financial promotions, rate offers, IPO marketing, generic investment opportunities, and optional customer-feedback surveys are not Personal. Booking confirmations, receipts, operational travel updates, and specific account/security/transaction/credit-change alerts remain Personal. Generic re-engagement summaries and “what you missed” messages are not Personal. Classify message-by-message: a service may send both useful Personal notices and promotional junk. Excludes unsolicited bulk social-network digests, trending-post notifications, generic recommendations, and engagement bait. Guardian insurance messages about claims, coverage, billing, plan documents, account changes, or required benefits actions are Personal. Specific dental reminders, requested estimates, and concrete credit/account changes are Personal.
criteria.work: Professional or technical correspondence, conferences, recruiters, colleagues, business, or industry matters tied to the recipient’s professional relationships or responsibilities. A person-specific professional invitation or direct message relayed by a platform may qualify. Generic automated invitation summaries, engagement reminders, or network-growth nags do not. School communications are Work only when the recipient is acting as an employee, vendor, or professional—not as a parent or family member. Excludes recurring author-led broadcast letters or essays that are not specifically about the recipient, even when they discuss technology, work, or business.
criteria.github: Any notification delivered by GitHub about repositories, account security, tokens, issues, pull requests, commits, reviews, actions, releases, or discussions.
criteria.email_lists: A genuine discussion mailing list supported by a List-ID or known list address, plus administrative mail about subscribing, unsubscribing, confirmations, command results, or delivery failures for such lists. Excludes social-network and ordinary service notifications.
criteria.newsletters: Recurring author-led broadcast letters or essays from an identifiable individual person, written in that person’s personal first-person voice and primarily intended to be read. They feel like one person writing to an audience in a friend-like, conversational way and remain newsletters when discussing technology, work, or business. The sender/byline must identify the individual author. Company names, brands, teams, editorial staffs, institutions, and corporate publications never qualify, even when content-first. An identifiable person or newsletter platform alone is insufficient: product launches, vendor announcements, branded pitches, sponsored content, and promotional posts are not Newsletters. Established recurring editorial weeklies curated by an identifiable individual, such as JavaScript Weekly, qualify when their purpose is editorial reading rather than corporate/product marketing.
criteria.potential_spam: Legitimate or plausibly legitimate but unwanted bulk, feed, acquisition, promotion, recommendation, or re-engagement content. Includes recurring account-based digests, recommendations, activity summaries, and content roundups from social networks, forums, and feed-driven services; Reddit digests; all Nextdoor neighborhood posts and digests; unsolicited marketing; discounts; product updates; cold sales; recruiting blasts; company-branded publications; corporate editorial content; brand or team-authored newsletters; financial-product promotions, rate offers, and IPO marketing; optional post-purchase, post-stay, post-appointment, and customer-feedback survey requests; unsolicited product launches, vendor announcements, branded pitches, and promotional posts even when sent by an individual or through Substack; generic weekly recaps from commercial or financial services unless they report specific requested account activity; generic re-engagement messages using language such as “we miss you,” “come back,” “catch up,” or “what you missed”; generic social-platform invitation nags; automated LinkedIn profile, position, recommendation, summary, engagement, and generic invitation notifications; and commercial recommendations based on browsing or prior interest. Classify message-by-message rather than trusting the sender: the same service may send useful Personal transactional alerts and separate promotional fluff. Do not use for a genuine person-specific invitation, direct message, or specific user-requested account/activity alert. Also includes broad recurring consumer-service reports, club monthly or weekly roundups, prayer-request subscription feeds, automated home-value reports, every terms/privacy-policy update, App Store Connect analytics summaries, all LinkedIn invitation notifications, and generic Guardian wellness or EAP promotions.
criteria.spam: Clearly deceptive, fraudulent, malicious, or worthless junk. Includes phishing, fake invoices, fabricated accounts or rewards, random-domain casino offers, fake dating messages, adult bait, miracle-cure claims, impersonation, and similar scam patterns.

needs_action.instructions: Only email categorized as personal or work can require action. For every other category, choose no. For personal or work, decide whether the recipient has a legitimate reason or obligation to act; ignore actions serving only the sender’s marketing, sales, or fraudulent goal.

criteria.yes: The category is personal or work, and a reply is genuinely expected or the recipient must decide, pay, schedule, provide information, review assigned work, meet a deadline, or resolve a legitimate account or security issue.
criteria.no: The category is not personal or work, or the message is informational or optional. Includes advertisements, promotions, discounts, newsletters, product announcements, GitHub notifications, email lists, scams, phishing, unsubscribe links, and generic calls to click, buy, register, deposit, claim, or learn more.

urgency.instructions: Assign urgency independently of whether action is required. Choose high only for legitimate immediate urgency; choose low for legitimate attention needed within several days; otherwise choose none. Spam, potential_spam, marketing, fabricated scarcity, and optional informational mail always have none.

criteria.high: Highest urgency: someone is blocked, immediate intervention is needed, or a real deadline or security risk is within 24 hours.
criteria.low: Needs legitimate attention within several days, but nobody is currently blocked and it is not immediately urgent.
criteria.none: No meaningful time pressure; informational, optional, routine, marketing, spam, potential spam, or fabricated urgency.
